headline: High: n8n’s server-side write/network privileges can cascade into document-processing actions, while shared workflow state creates prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance risks with PaddleOCR.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools via workflow nodes, so attacker-controlled document content from PaddleOCR can be routed into downstream prompts or nodes. PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can be used as an input source. The shared workflow path is plausible, though not proven to be a direct parser hijack.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is inserted into an n8n AI Agent prompt or node input without sanitization
IF the workflow reads untrusted documents from a shared filesystem path
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/template around OCR text before prompt use
Insert a manual review step before any AI Agent node consumes OCR output
Restrict n8n file inputs to a dedicated staging directory
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to OCR outputs and enforce them in workflow nodes

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and has broad network egress plus server filesystem access, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If sensitive documents are OCR’d and then passed through n8n integrations, leakage can occur through workflow logs, API nodes, or credentialed connectors. The pair does not show a built-in isolation boundary.
conditions: IF the workflow processes sensitive documents or images
IF n8n sends OCR text to an external integration node or logs it
mitigations: Disable verbose workflow logging for document payloads
Limit OCR inputs to non-sensitive test data until reviewed
Use per-workflow credentials with least privilege
Mask or redact document text before any outbound API call
requires-engineering: add data-class routing rules for sensitive documents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n has server filesystem write and broad egress, while PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and browser execution. If both operate on the same shared workspace or mutable document set, they can overwrite or race on files and outputs. No locking or coordination primitive is documented in either profile, so conflict risk is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or document set
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access to shared files
mitigations: Assign separate input/output directories per agent
Use immutable filenames for OCR artifacts
Add a quick lock file or lease check before writes
Run one agent at a time on shared documents
requires-engineering: implement workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate downstream actions, and PaddleOCR produces extracted document text that n8n may treat as authoritative input. If OCR errors or prompt-injected text are forwarded into workflow actions, n8n can execute incorrect or irreversible operations. The pair lacks a documented verification gate, so the cascade is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF OCR output is used as the source of truth for downstream workflow decisions
IF n8n triggers external actions such as emails, API writes, or file updates from that output
mitigations: Add a human approval step before any irreversible action
Require schema validation on OCR output fields
Compare OCR results against a second extraction pass for critical documents
Log confidence scores and block low-confidence records
requires-engineering: add policy checks before action nodes

E_compliance.rationale: n8n stores secrets on its server and processes whatever the workflow handles, while PaddleOCR is a document-processing component with no stated residency or retention controls. If EU PII or regulated documents flow through n8n workflows, retention and residency mismatches are plausible. The profiles do not prove a violation, but the compliance boundary is undocumented.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated documents or EU personal data
IF n8n retention, logging, or hosting location differs from the source-data policy
mitigations: Confirm where n8n stores workflow logs and credentials
Disable retention of raw OCR payloads where possible
Route regulated documents only through approved environments
Document a data-processing agreement for any external hosting
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
